sentence_stem: Had the team prepared more thoroughly,
correct_completion: they would have won the match.
full_sentence: Had the team prepared more thoroughly, they would have won the match.
acceptable_variants: they would have scored more goals.
they might have won the match.

options.text: they would win the match now.
options.why_wrong: The inverted third conditional refers to an unreal past, so 'now' conflicts with the past time frame set by 'had prepared'.

options.text: they will have won the match.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' is used for real future possibilities, but this sentence describes an imagined result of an unreal past condition.

options.text: they would have won the match.

options.why_wrong: This states a plain past fact rather than the imagined result of a condition that did not happen.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (had + past participle, then would have + past participle)
explanation: Inverted conditionals drop 'if' and move 'had' to the front of the clause. The main clause then needs 'would have' followed by a past participle. Learners who come from a language with a suffix-based past conditional often simplify this to a plain past or to 'would' alone, which loses the past reference.
translation: Takım daha titiz hazırlanmış olsaydı, maçı kazanmış olurdu.
